questions.q: The article calls one kind of conduct a “knee-jerk character.” What is it?
options: Obeying rules without thought
Not quite. The article says: Simply returning the treatment one receives – good for good, harm for harm.
Changing one’s mind often
Not quite. The article says: Simply returning the treatment one receives – good for good, harm for harm.
Acting without any feeling
Not quite. The article says: Simply returning the treatment one receives – good for good, harm for harm.
Simply returning the treatment one receives – good for good, harm for harm
Yes. A high character does not depend on how others behave.
questions.rationale: “An ordinary character is based on the principle: ‘Do as you have been done by.’ This might be termed a ‘Knee-jerk character.’”

Not quite. The article says: Setting the same standard for oneself as for others, and treating the weak with the courtesy shown to the strong.

options: He wore the new one for the journey
Not quite. The article says: He returned it and kept his own, saying it absorbed sweat better.
He returned it and kept his own, saying it absorbed sweat better
Yes. A lesson in humility and contentment.

Not quite. The article says: He returned it and kept his own, saying it absorbed sweat better.

Not quite. The article says: He returned it and kept his own, saying it absorbed sweat better.

As an opportunity for reflection and preparation for the Hereafter, not for lament

Not quite. The article says: As an opportunity for reflection and preparation for the Hereafter, not for lament.
